articles.title: 'Salty' RJ Barrett Reacts to Knicks Winning NBA Title After Trade to Raptors in OG Anunoby Deal
articles.summary: RJ Barrett started his NBA career with the New York Knicks after they selected him with the No. 3 overall pick of the 2019 draft, and he was "happy" they won the championship even if he was feeling a little "salty" because his Toronto Raptors lost in the playoffs.
articles.body:
RJ Barrett started his NBA career with the New York Knicks after they selected him with the No. 3 overall pick of the 2019 draft, and he was "happy" they won the championship even if he was feeling a little "salty" because his Toronto Raptors lost in the playoffs.

"At first, definitely feel a little salty in terms of we lost, the Raptors lost in the first round, so that hurt," he said during an interview with CBC Sports (4:55 mark) when discussing the team that traded him to Toronto to acquire OG Anunoby. "But if anybody else were to win it, I'm happy they won it. I still have friends over there. I've called and checked on the guys, said congrats.

5 NBA Stars Who Could Dominate Trade Rumors 🤔

"One of the guys from the team is actually on the Raptors now, so things are cool. The mayor gave myself a quick a shout-out, so we'll always have ties there. I'm very happy for them, but hoping to bring some of that success over here."

That one player who was on the Knicks last year and joined Toronto was Trey Jemison lll, who signed a two-way contract with the Raptors this offseason.

As for Barrett, he played well during his tenure with the Knicks, averaging 18.1 points, 5.3 rebounds and 2.8 assists a night over the course of 297 games from 2019-20 until they traded him during the 2023-24 campaign.

However, New York never made it past the second round of the playoffs during his tenure and moved him as part of a roster overhaul that also included adding Karl-Anthony Towns to the frontcourt.

The Barrett trade ended up being particularly important in the Knicks' championship run, as they landed Anunoby from the Raptors as part of the deal. Anunoby was arguably the team's top defender throughout the regular season and playoffs and then played the role of hero in Game 4 of the NBA Finals against the San Antonio Spurs with the winning tip-in at the end.

New York's championship came after Barrett's Raptors lost in the first round to the Cleveland Cavaliers in seven games. It was a step in the right direction for Toronto after missing the playoffs the previous three seasons, and it could be a threat in the Eastern Conference during the 2026-27 campaign with the addition of Kawhi Leonard.

Perhaps the Raptors will even face the Knicks in a playoff series, which would provide another motivating factor for Barrett.

articles.title: Countdown to Practice #1: Preston Edmead
articles.summary: Our point guard Coach’s first point guard
articles.body:
Welcome to the Preseason – Basketball practice officially starts TOMORROW!

Now what EXACTLY does 'basketball practice officially starts' mean? The 'Master of all things college basketball' (the NCAA) says practice officially starts 42 days prior to the first scheduled game. It is traditionally the six weeks where the individual workouts end and the 'systems' are installed. This season, that date falls on September 21. But during a September 9 th interview with Assistant Coach Matt Driscoll we got a sneak peek under the covers when he said:

"We're in a really good place going into opening practice, but in reality, practice started August 17 th ". (first day of fall classes)

We're counting down the 10 days to the beginning of practice '26-'27 by taking another look at this season's roster, focusing on the 10 players most likely to make an impact. This last article is about a player I believe will be one of the most exciting in the ACC, Preston Edmead.

Predicted breakdown of minutes per player:

Preston was unheralded coming out of high school, but is a 4-star transfer, ranked #156 from Easthampton, MA, via Hofstra. He's got a NC connection; his big brother Aaren played in Greensboro at NC A&T '17-'18 and '18-'19. He played his freshman season at Hofstra. He was the CAA Rookie of the Year , Second Team All-CAA , CAA All-Rookie team and was the CAA Championship Game's Most Outstanding Player .

PPG / RPG / APG: 16.1 ppg / 3.5 rpg / 4.4 apg

Shooting: 40.1% / 38.7% (96-248) / 83.3%

Points: 26 points, 29 games in double figures, 10 games with 20+

3PT Shooting: 13 games making 4+ 3PT shots

Hit 6 3PT shots in their NCAA tournament game against Alabama

Assists: 9 assists (2x), 16 games with 5+

Let's look a little closer using CBB Analytics :

Preston is a high-usage, and simultaneously high-quality, offensive player. Green lights across the board.

Rebounding – His stats look bad (19 th percentile), but when compared to only guards his per game defensive rebounding average (2.8) is 75% percentile.

Quality shooter – 3PT and FT are in the 80 th percentiles

Only 7% of his points were fast break points last season

His game is going to be primarily the 3PT shot or the assist. Last season he did okay with mid-range jumpers – Hammond is elite at that – but once he got within about 10 feet of the basket, it was bad news. But that's okay. This season he will be playing with two guys that are elite within 10 feet of the basket.

College Basketball Report released its ranking of the Top 30 sophomores in college basketball heading into the 2026-27 season, and Edmead checked in at No. 29 nationally .

Matthew Winick (college basketball analyst)

"Outside his teammate Cruz Davis, Edmead was probably the best guard in the CAA last year… but Davis was in his fourth year of CBB and Edmead in his first. Uber-impressive. Great passer, tremendous PNR player, you want to run your team through him. He's also exceptionally clutch. Has it all as an on-ball star PG except for the rim, he's REALLY small and that impacts his ability to score on non-threes."

"One of the best off-the-dribble shooters in the country; he's going to blow the roof off Lenovo; there's going to be a lot of kids trying to emulate Preston Edmead"

"I've been impressed with his toughness, his edge"

"Preston Edmead is a junk yard dog [on defense]. He is as tough as they come. He will apply pressure and the other guys have got to have his back. We'll be in the gaps and making it tough to get paint access. That's where it all starts."

Expectations – Preston Edmead is an excellent basketball player and will be a fan favorite. He's only a sophomore, if he sticks around he's going to sell a lot of #0 jerseys.

3PT Shooting – Preston is an elite, off-the-dribble 3PT shooter. Patrick Stacy predicts he's going to have multiple 30-point games this season at Lenovo. And he might be right. Here's some numbers that will get your juices flowing. Paul McNeil took 246 3PT attempts last season (T- 52 nd in NCAA) and made 105 (T-55 th in NCAA) at an excellent 42.7%. (18 th in NCAA) Preston took 248 3PT attempts last season (T-46 th in NCAA) and made 96 (T- 30 th in NCAA) at 38.8%. (63 rd in NCAA) Paul's strength is catch-and-shoot. Preston's strength is shooting off the dribble. And they will be on the court at the same time most of this season.

Assists – Hofstra was an interesting team last season with basically two point guards. Cruz Davis, the actual point guard, was a senior and led the team in assists with 164 (2 nd in the CAA) averaging 4.7 apg. (2 nd in the CAA) Impressively, freshman Preston was right behind him with 154 assists (3 rd in the CAA, #86 in NCAA) averaging 4.4 apg (4 th in the CAA). Davis gets the quantity nod, but Preston gets the quality nod, he averaged an impressive Assist/Turnover ration of 2.0 (tied for 4 th in the CAA) and he is excellent with the PNR. This season, with all the quality shooters on this team, he's going to thrive.

Is he a actually a point guard? – Yes. Recruiting listed him as a point guard coming out of high school. But last season Hofstra needed a shooting guard, and he did it well. In the CAA championship game he led both teams in minutes played (40) and points (26) and they won. So, he has some work to do on his point guard game – but, he's only a sophomore, and we know a guy.

Can he do it against P4 competition? – Survey says, Yes! Hofstra played Alabama in the first round of the NCAAT last season. Preston played 40 minutes and scored 24 points (6/13 from 3PT – 46.2%), 4 rebounds, and 4 assists. However, he also turned it over 4 times and shot only 3/12 (25%) from 2PT. Earlier in the season Hofstra beat both Pitt, Preston had 8 pts (8-9 FT) / 2 reb / 4 assist, and Syracuse, Preston had 12 pts (4-6 from 3PT) / 0 reb / 1 assist.

Defensively, Coach Gainey is saying good things about him in practice. (" junk yard dog ") But like most of the guys on this team, he's got work to do.

So what are we going to see this season? He's going to start at point guard. He's fast. He's aggressive. He's a very confident ball handler. He will lead the team in scoring some nights. He's a lot of fun to watch, and he's only a sophomore. Buy that #0 jersey early, they'll sell out.

articles.summary: The EuroLeague tips off Thursday with three former Bulldogs on rosters. Here's where and what to expect from each.
articles.body:
Eighteen former Zags played professional basketball outside the United States in 2025-26. Mario Saint-Supery joined them on July 11, when he left Gonzaga after one season to sign with Valencia Basket in Spain. The group is spread across Spain, France, Italy, Lithuania, Japan and the United Arab Emirates, among other places.

Nigel Williams-Goss, Filip Petrusev and Saint-Supery all play for EuroLeague clubs in 2026-27. At 32, Williams-Goss is the oldest of the three, a point guard for Žalgiris Kaunas who won the EuroLeague with Real Madrid in 2023. Petrusev, 26, plays for Dubai Basketball, the reigning ABA League champion, and won his own EuroLeague title in 2022 with Anadolu Efes. Saint-Supery is the youngest at 20, and Valencia has him under contract through June 30, 2030.

The Euroleague season just tipped off and the Gonzaga pipeline is well represented at the highest levels this season. Here's a brief check-in on how each of these former Zags is faring in their Euroleague homes and what fans can expect from them this season.

Žalgiris opened the 2026-27 LKL season today at Neptūnas, and Williams-Goss takes the floor as the unambiguous lead guard of a team that lost its best player over the summer. Sylvain Francisco, All-EuroLeague First Team last year at 16.5 points and 6.5 assists per game, bought out his contract and signed with Panathinaikos. That's a real vacancy. The replacement piece is Jonas Valanciunas, 14 years in the NBA before Denver waived him, who looked like himself in preseason — 14 points and 9 rebounds against Juventus — and gives Žalgiris a frontcourt anchor it hasn't had. In that same game, Williams-Goss ran the offense quietly: 6 points, 6 assists, the right kind of preseason line for a 32-year-old point guard managing his minutes before a long year.

He'll need them. The EuroLeague opener comes Thursday at Crvena Zvezda, then Žalgiris hosts Olympiacos — his former club, the reigning champion — on September 29. He's spent a career collecting hardware in places American fans don't watch closely: a EuroLeague title with Real Madrid in 2023, the Lithuanian league with Žalgiris last spring, four straight Final Fours before Fenerbahçe knocked them out in the quarterfinals in May. The body is the variable. Three soft-tissue injuries interrupted his first Kaunas season, but when healthy he was the best version of himself in Europe, and this roster — built around him and Valanciunas — has the bones to go deeper than last year if he stays on the floor.

The story of Petrusev's first year in Dubai was partly buried under a knee that he described, at 26, as feeling like it belonged to a 36-year-old. He played all 38 EuroLeague games anyway, averaged 11.6 points and 4.8 rebounds, and helped the club win the ABA League title in just its second season of existence. By the end he was running on injections and painkillers, grinding through cartilage damage and two bone edemas in his right knee severe enough that he admitted publicly this summer there was barely any cartilage left in certain spots. The fact that he suited up in last weekend's EuroLeague SuperCup third-place game against Fenerbahçe and scored 7 points as a starter is either a good sign or a sign that he'll play through anything.

He's 26, has a EuroLeague ring from his year at Anadolu Efes and an Olympic bronze from Paris with Serbia, and enters year two in Dubai as the frontcourt anchor for a team that just swapped coaches (Golemac out in April, Xavi Pascual in) and added former Virginia star Mamadi Diakite alongside him up front. The roster is deeper and the EuroLeague opener is Thursday at home against Real Madrid. Petrusev told Italian media this week that the preparation has been ideal and that the only way to grow is to test yourself against the best. Whether his knee allows him to do that over the course of a full season is the real question going into 2026-27.

Mario Saint-Supery left Gonzaga after one season, and then suddenly announced just two days after shaking hands and posing for photo-ops at the Domantas Sabonis Strength and Conditioning Center dedication ceremony that he was taking a four-year, $15 million deal with Valencia Basket. He was back in Spain later that week.

He told the Spanish press that the EuroLeague is "the best league in the world after the NBA," which is the kind of thing you say when you'd like everyone to stop asking why you bailed on a top-10 NCAA program that made you its starting point guard as a freshman. Valencia made the EuroLeague Final Four last year and won the Liga ACB, then spent the summer watching Jean Montero leave for Olympiacos and Sergio de Larrea go 25th in the NBA Draft, so Saint-Supery arrives as the replacement plan for two players who are considerably better than him, behind a 35-year-old Nikola Mirotic on a roster that looks considerably worse than last year's.

For Zag fans who want to track all three at once, the schedule serves up six Gonzaga alumni matchups across the season. Williams-Goss and Petrusev meet twice — December 4 in Kaunas and April 7 in Dubai. Williams-Goss and Saint-Supery face off December 23 in Kaunas and March 4 in Valencia. Petrusev and Saint-Supery meet December 15 in Valencia and March 10 in Dubai. Circle December 23 in particular: that's the one where an all-time fan favorite Gonzaga point guard in Williams-Goss gets to play against an all-time Gonzaga fan-least-favorite in Lithuania. That one will air somewhere around noon Pacific time for anyone willing to find the stream.

articles.title: Olivia Miles passes Caitlin Clark for most points scored in a WNBA rookie season
articles.summary: Olivia Miles made history on Sunday, passing Caitlin Clark two years after her Rookie of the Year season.
articles.body:
The WNBA has a new name atop its record book. On Sunday, Minnesota Lynx rookie Olivia Miles surpassed Caitlin Clark for the league's single-season rookie points record.

The record-breaking moment came on a free throw in the second quarter of the Lynx's matchup against the Connecticut Sun , marking Miles' 770th point of the season.

Clark set the record during her Rookie of the Year campaign in 2024, finishing the season with 769 points and passing Hall of Famer Seimone Augustus' 744 points from 2006. Miles has been the clear frontrunner for 2026 Rookie of the Year all season, but this record-breaking moment appears to make her grip on that award even tighter.

Miles tied Clark's mark in a 20-point performance against the New York Liberty on Friday; after a slow start, Miles scored nine points in the fourth quarter to come one point away from breaking the record. The Lynx went on to lose to New York, 93-81 .

Though Clark's 2024 record came when the WNBA played 40 games, the league has since expanded to 44 games in the regular season. However, Miles, who missed two games with a calf injury in July, notably reached the achievement in her 40th game of the season, matching Clark's mark in the same number of games.

Miles, who was selected by the Lynx No. 2 overall out of TCU, has been on an absolute tear in her rookie season. "The Spectacle" hopped in as an immediate starter, averaging nearly 20 points per game; she sits in the top 10 league-wide in points and assists per game, despite being just 23.

Minnesota is still in play for the No. 1 seed over the Golden State Valkyries , but Friday night's loss didn't help. The Lynx will need to win their next two games, or hope for a Valkyries loss, in order to finally secure that top spot.

articles.title: Olivia Miles Breaks Caitlin Clark's Scoring Record, Makes WNBA History During Rookie Season for Lynx
articles.summary: Minnesota Lynx star Olivia Miles made history in Sunday's game against the Connecticut sun.
articles.body:
Minnesota Lynx star Olivia Miles made history in Sunday's game against the Connecticut sun.

The All-Star guard scored her 770th and 771st points of the 2026 WNBA season, breaking the rookie record set by the Indiana Fever's Caitlin Clark in 2024.

A lot of single-season marks have fallen over the last few years with the WNBA expanding the schedule. Clark made three more appearances than Seimone Augustus when she set the rookie scoring mark in 2006.

Sunday was Miles' 40th game, matching Clark's total from 2024.

It's not as if the former Notre Dame and TCU standout flew under the radar coming into the 2026 WNBA draft. She almost certainly would've been a lottery pick in 2025 if she had declared, and she solidified her stock during her lone season with the Horned Frogs.

Nobody foresaw Miles making the kind of impact she has, though. Entering Sunday, she was averaging 19.7 points on 48.8 percent shooting along with 4.7 rebounds, 5.9 assists and 1.3 steals.

Beyond the raw numbers, Miles has influenced winning basketball in a way you typically don't see from first-year players, especially first-year guards. Minnesota owned the league's best record (21-6) before franchise cornerstone Napheesa Collier finally returned from injury on July 22.

Were it not for the Las Vegas Aces' A'ja Wilson, Miles would probably be the MVP favorite. Alas, she'll have to settle for Rookie of the Year and a first team All-WNBA nod.

The regular season will increase from 44 games to 50 starting in 2027, so Miles' scoring record may not hold forever. But she's having the kind of debut campaign that will be remembered for a long time.

articles.title: Before winning six NBA championships, Michael Jordan faced high school rejection that fuelled his rise to basketball greatness
articles.summary: NBA News: Michael Jordan is widely regarded as one of the greatest basketball players of all time. His name is synonymous with championships, record-breaking pe.
articles.body: Michael Jordan is widely regarded as one of the greatest basketball players of all time. His name is synonymous with championships, record-breaking performances and an unmatched competitive spirit. However, his journey to becoming a global sports icon was not always smooth. Before he became the face of the Chicago Bulls and transformed basketball into a worldwide phenomenon, Jordan faced rejection, setbacks and moments of self-doubt.Michael Jordan's early life and the setback that fuelled his ambitionBorn in Brooklyn, New York, on February 17, 1963, Michael Jordan grew up in Wilmington, North Carolina, in a working-class family. His rise from a young basketball enthusiast to an NBA legend is a powerful reminder that early setbacks do not have to define a person's future. Instead, they can become the motivation needed to achieve extraordinary success.Jordan developed a passion for sports during childhood. He enjoyed basketball, baseball and football, but basketball eventually became his primary focus. His competitive nature was evident from an early age, and he constantly looked for ways to improve his performance.One of the most frequently discussed moments in Jordan's early basketball journey occurred during his sophomore year at Laney High School in Wilmington. He did not make the varsity basketball team and was instead assigned to the junior varsity squad.The experience became a major source of motivation for the young athlete. Although the story is often simplified as a rejection based on his height, Jordan was still developing physically and competing for a limited number of varsity positions. The setback nevertheless left a lasting impression on him.Rather than giving up, Jordan used the disappointment as motivation to improve. He practised relentlessly, worked on his skills and developed the determination that would later become a defining feature of his career.Jordan eventually earned a place on the varsity team and continued to improve as a player. His high school performances attracted attention from college basketball programmes, opening the door to the next stage of his journey.Michael Jordan's college career opened the door to the NBAJordan joined the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill in 1981, where he played under legendary coach Dean Smith. The college programme helped him develop his basketball fundamentals, discipline and understanding of the game.His defining college moment came during the 1982 NCAA championship game against Georgetown. Jordan made the game-winning jump shot, helping North Carolina secure the national title. The performance introduced him to a wider basketball audience and marked an important milestone in his development.Jordan continued to establish himself as one of the country's leading college players. His scoring ability, athleticism and competitive drive made him a highly anticipated prospect for the NBA.In 1984, the Chicago Bulls selected Jordan with the third overall pick in the NBA Draft. His arrival in Chicago marked the beginning of a professional career that would eventually reshape the franchise and influence basketball around the world.Jordan made an immediate impact during his rookie season, earning the NBA Rookie of the Year award. His explosive playing style, scoring ability and confidence quickly made him one of the league's most exciting young stars.Michael Jordan's Chicago Bulls era changed basketball historyJordan's early NBA years established him as an elite player, but winning an NBA championship proved more challenging. The Chicago Bulls faced difficult playoff battles, including repeated losses to the Detroit Pistons.Those defeats tested Jordan's patience and determination. Instead of allowing frustration to derail his ambitions, he continued to refine his game and strengthen his physical conditioning.The breakthrough finally came in 1991, when Jordan led the Bulls to their first NBA championship by defeating the Los Angeles Lakers. Chicago went on to win three consecutive titles from 1991 to 1993, establishing itself as one of the league's dominant teams.Jordan shocked the basketball world in 1993 when he announced his retirement from the NBA and pursued professional baseball. Although his baseball career did not reach the same heights as his basketball achievements, the experience became another unusual chapter in his sporting journey.He returned to the NBA in 1995 and soon helped Chicago reclaim its place at the top. The Bulls won three more consecutive championships from 1996 to 1998, completing a second three-peat.Jordan finished his Bulls career with six NBA championships, five regular-season MVP awards and six NBA Finals MVP awards. His performances during the championship years helped cement his reputation as one of basketball's most accomplished players.Michael Jordan's legacy goes beyond championships and fameJordan's influence extended far beyond the basketball court. His partnership with Nike helped turn the Air Jordan brand into a major force in sportswear and popular culture. The shoes became a symbol of athletic excellence and style, reaching audiences well beyond basketball fans.His global popularity also played a significant role in expanding the NBA's international appeal. Jordan's performances, competitive personality and memorable championship runs attracted new generations of fans around the world.In 2009, Jordan was inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame, recognising his extraordinary contributions to the sport.His career also offers a powerful lesson about perseverance. Jordan's journey was not a simple rise from talent to fame. It involved rejection, difficult losses, demanding training and the willingness to keep improving.The high school setback that once disappointed him became part of a much larger story about determination and personal growth. Jordan's success was built not only on natural ability but also on discipline, resilience and an unrelenting desire to improve.Michael Jordan's journey from a young player in North Carolina to a global basketball icon shows that setbacks do not have to determine the outcome of a person's life. His legacy continues to inspire athletes and fans to work through challenges, learn from failure and pursue their ambitions with determination.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Resume triple talaq study: NCW to Keralam govt
articles.summary: NCW urges Kerala to resume Malappuram triple talaq impact study, asks chief secretary to intervene and submit action taken report within 7 days.
articles.body: THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: National Commission for Women (NCW) has asked Keralam govt to withdraw the pause on the proposed study on the socio-legal impact of triple talaq among Muslim women in Malappuram. It sought chief secretary’s personal intervention to let the fieldwork proceed and file an action taken report within seven days.NCW member secretary Sudeep Jain’s letter to chief secretary Bishwanath Sinha on Sept 15 referred to the “reported decision” of the state govt to put the fieldwork on hold, despite state authorities having earlier agreed to facilitate it. NCW’s direct request to govt to withdraw the pause on the study marks a fresh turn in the issue.Jain pointed out that NCW had sought Malappuram district collector’s cooperation on July 1 and women and child development (WCD) department’s on July 20. “No legal, administrative or methodological objection was communicated, and the department had conveyed its willingness to assist,” the letter said.The study, commissioned under Section 10 of National Commission for Women Act, 1990, covers selected districts in Jammu & Kashmir, Assam, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar and Keralam. It seeks to assess the lived experiences of women affected by triple talaq, the socio-legal impact of the law and the adequacy of support mechanisms.Keralam’s participation is important not only for understanding conditions within the state but also for ensuring that the study presents a balanced national picture and produces lessons relevant to policy and implementation across the country, NCW said.“This independent academic study safeguards confidentiality and informed participation. It neither seeks the state govt’s endorsement nor interferes with its administration,” the letter said.NCW said excluding one of the selected states would weaken the national evidence base and the study’s comparability.“If any specific concern exists, it may kindly be conveyed to the commission in writing with reasons,” said the letter.The development follows state WCD directorate’s earlier communication to Malappuram district administration that necessary assistance could be extended to the research team. Govt subsequently decided to keep the matter in abeyance.A senior official of minority welfare department said govt was examining the matter. “Since it involves field-level data collection among a particular section of the population in a specific district, govt would like to consider all relevant aspects before taking a final decision,” the official said.Govt’s decision to keep the study in abeyance assumes significance as Malappuram is the only district in Keralam specifically identified for primary data collection under the multi-state study. NCW’s letter says the project covers selected districts in six states, while the Keralam component involves data collection from affected Muslim women in Malappuram.Stay updated with the latest Thiruvananthapuram news. articles.title: Un Laprovittola sublime ejecuta al Barça y da un título al Joventut 18 años después
articles.standfirst: El argentino prolonga la sequía de sus ex (3 años y 3 meses sin levantar trofeos) con una actuación colosal: 31 puntos con 9/13 triples y 7 asistencias en 22 minutos
articles.summary: El argentino prolonga la sequía de sus ex azulgranas con 31 puntos y 9/13 triples
articles.body: El Barça enseñó la puerta de salida a Nico Laprovittola al final de la pasada temporada. Le había dado muchas tardes de gloria, pero a sus 36 años su prioridad era rejuvenecer su plantilla. Lo que seguro que no esperaba era que apenas tres meses después el genial base argentino le ejecutase (101-87) alargando su sequía (tres años y tres meses sin levantar trofeos) para coronar al Joventut en la final de la Supercopa Endesa con un partido memorable. La suya fue la venganza del ex elevada al infinito. Inició el partido como suplente, pero cuando saltó a la cancha tardó muy poco en demostrar que iba a ser el jugador de la final, convirtiendo casi todos los lanzamientos que intentó para desesperación del Barça. Acabó con 31 puntos (1/3 t2, 9/13 triples y 2/2 tl.), 2 rebotes, 7 asistencias y 28 de valoración en poco más de 22 minutos en cancha. Fue el héroe indiscutible de una Penya que levantó su primer trofeo en los últimos 18 años, desde que en 2008 conquistase la Copa ULEB y la Copa del Rey. Una interminable travesía por el desierto que acabó, no podía ser de otra forma, en medio del delirio de un Olímpico de Badalona que reverdeció viejos laureles mientras elevaba a Laprovittola al olimpo de sus dioses históricos. Su retorno al Joventut no podía ser más exitoso, pero no solo del argentino vivieron los verdinegros, propulsados también por la solvencia de Ricky Rubio (10+2+8), Eli Ndiaye (14+3+2) y Emir Sulejmanovic (19+9). Ellos fueron los grandes complementos del recital histórico de su compañero. No en vano, batió el récord de triples en una edición de la Supercopa con 14 anotados (5/10 en la semifinal y 9/13 en la final), contribuyendo a que su equipo también superase la plusmarca de triples en el torneo. El gran damnificado de su acierto fue un Barça al que no le bastó el empeño de Parra (24), Punter (20) y Martin (16) para sobrevivir al ciclón argentino. El Joventut conjuró la agresividad defensiva y la supremacía física de su rival con la magia de Ricky Rubio y Nico Laprovittola, dos jugones con poco músculo pero mucho cerebro que hicieron bueno el dicho que más vale maña que fuerza. Ellos llevaron al límite al Barça, dejando en evidencia su defensa hasta el descanso (50-46) tras un inicio de partido en el que ofrecieron un clinic de baloncesto (37-27, min 12). Ricky, con 7 puntos y 4 asistencias, demostró desde el salto inicial que su Penya iba a por el título. Y lo ratificó Laprovittola saliendo desde el banquillo con 12 puntos (4/5 t3) y dos asistencias en apenas cinco minutos. El Barça apretó las clavijas en defensa y se acercó en el marcador gracias a Parra y Brizuela (39-36). Pero el omnipresente Laprovittola abortó la reacción con otros dos triples (50-41). Por entonces llevaba ya 18 puntos (6/7 triples). Punter, otro jugón algo aletargado, despertó con dos tiros libres y un triple para acercar al Barça antes del descanso (50-46, min 20). No cejó en su empeño el Joventut, que puso la máxima con un espléndido Reyes (61-48, min 23). Los triples de Parra y Punter sacaron del coma a los azulgranas, que se echaron encima de su rival con otro arreón antes del final del tercer cuarto propulsados por dos jugadas de tres puntos de Martin, un triple de Punter y una canasta sobre la bocina de Robinson (71-68, min 30). Fue todo lo que logró inquietar el Barça, que no tuvo una sola ventaja en todo el partido, ya que de nuevo apareció Laprovittola para ampliar la renta de seguridad de los suyos con dos tiros libres y su séptimo triple (82-72, min 33). Y tres minutos después apuntilló a sus ex con su octavo y su noveno triple (94-84, min 39) levantando de sus asientos a un Olímpico de Badalona que vivió un éxtasis que ya no recordaban ni los más viejos del lugar. ¡Qué bueno que volviste!, debieron pensar. 101. Asisa Joventut (32+20+19+30): Rubio (10), Ellis (8), Reyes (11), Ndiaye (14), Sulejmanovic (19) -cinco inicial-; Kraag (4), Laprovittola (31), Hakanson (-), Torres (-), Nogués (-), Birgander (2) y Cheatham (2). 87. Barça: (23+23+22+19): Robinson (8), Punter (20), Umude (2), Parra (24), Nebo (3) -cinco inicial-; Gibson (-), Martin (16), Brizuela (6), Nkamhoua (5), Núñez (-), Balcerowski (3) y Minaya (-). Árbitros: Antonio Conde, Carlos Peruga y Arnau Padrós. Eliminaron por cinco faltas personales al jugador visitante Gibson (min. 25). Incidencias: Partido correspondiente a la final de la Supercopa Endesa disputado en el Palau Olímpic de Badalona ante 12.046 espectadores.

articles.title: Ricky Rubio se corona en la Penya 18 años después
articles.standfirst: Ricky, emocionado tras conquistar la Supercopa con Raúl Fuentes en Otra Ronda con Chitu.
articles.summary: Ricky, emocionado tras conquistar la Supercopa con Raúl Fuentes en Otra Ronda con Chitu.
articles.body: EEl Asisa Joventut vuelve a tocar el cielo. La Penya conquistó su primera Supercopa de España tras imponerse al Barça por 101-87 en el Olímpic, en una noche histórica para el club verdinegro. Dieciocho años después de su último título, la ULEB de 2008, el conjunto de Badalona vuelve a levantar un trofeo nacional y lo hace ante su eterno rival, arropado por una afición que llevaba demasiado tiempo esperando una celebración así. El gran protagonista fue Ricky Rubio. El base catalán tomó el mando desde el inicio y convirtió el partido en una exhibición de dirección, ritmo y liderazgo. Terminó con 10 puntos y 8 asistencias, aunque su impacto fue mucho mayor que lo reflejado en sus estadísticas. Rubio manejó los tiempos, encontró constantemente a sus compañeros y contagió al Olímpic de una energía que recordó a la gran Penya de otras épocas: "Ni en mis mejores sueños", reconoció después al recordar su regreso y la posibilidad de vivir una noche así en casa frente al Barça. A su lado apareció un Nikola Laprovittola absolutamente desatado. El argentino, de vuelta en Badalona después de su etapa en el Barça, fue elegido MVP de la Supercopa después de firmar una final extraordinaria: 31 puntos, 9 triples de 13 intentos y 7 asistencias. Seis de sus triples llegaron ya en la primera mitad, sosteniendo el dominio verdinegro y convirtiéndose en el principal ejecutor de una Penya que llegó a tener 13 puntos de ventaja en el tercer cuarto. Entre Ricky y Laprovittola protagonizaron buena parte del juego ofensivo de los locales. El Barça intentó reaccionar y llegó a colocarse a solo tres puntos al comienzo del último cuarto, pero el Joventut no perdió el control. La dirección de Rubio, el acierto exterior y la respuesta colectiva permitieron a los de Badalona cerrar el partido con autoridad. Los 17 triples anotados por la Penya establecieron además un nuevo récord en la historia de la competición. El triunfo supone el decimoquinto título nacional del Joventut y, sobre todo, devuelve al Olímpic una sensación que parecía lejana: la de ver a la Penya celebrar un gran trofeo: "Se tiene que disfrutar de momentos así porque hay pocos", resumió Ricky Rubio tras el partido. Dieciocho años después, Badalona vuelve a celebrar. Y lo hace con dos viejos conocidos, Ricky y Laprovittola, como protagonistas de una noche que ya forma parte de la historia verdinegra.

articles.title: Laprovittola: "Todo es gracias a mi familia y al equipo"
articles.standfirst: El héroe del Asisa Joventut admite que estaba especialmente motivado ante sus ex tras haberle 'cortado' en verano
articles.summary: El héroe del Asisa Joventut admite que estaba especialmente motivado ante sus ex tras haberle 'cortado' en verano
articles.body: Nico Laprovittola tenía una cuenta pendiente y decidió saldarla sobre la pista. El base argentino del Asisa Joventut fue coronado MVP de la Supercopa con una actuación descomunal en la final ante el Barça (101-87): 31 puntos y nueve triples para conquistar el título. Un partido especial para un jugador que este verano tuvo que hacer las maletas de Barcelona después de que el club azulgrana decidiera no renovarle. El propio Laprovittola reconoció que ese contexto le dio un plus de motivación. “Sin duda estaba más motivado. Me costó muchísimo asimilarlo este verano, pero son cosas que pasan y uno tiene que seguir. Estaba mucho más motivado de lo que el entrenador del Barça pensaba”. Su actuación, además, entró directamente en la historia de la Supercopa al batir el récord de triples en un partido, con nueve, superando los seis de su compatriota Pablo Prigioni en 2008. También estableció las mejores marcas de puntos (58) y triples (14) en una misma edición, sumando la semifinal y la final. “Todo es gracias a mi familia y al equipo. No sé como pasó, pero ahí estamos”, bromeó el argentino, que ha regresado a Badalona siete años después de abandonar la Penya. “Volver y que haya pasado esto no estaba en los planes. Sí pensaba que podíamos ganar desde el primer día que fiché, pero no la fiesta que hicimos este fin de semana. Ojalá todo se mantenga y sigamos creciendo. Ojalá esto nos dé un impulso muy grande”. También se emocionó con el triunfo Ricky Rubio que, como Laprovittola, está viviendo a sus 35 años una esplendorosa segunda juventud: "Tengo que reconocer que estaba más nervioso que en la final del Mundial de 2019. Para mí ganar un título aquí, después de tantos años, es espectacular. Estaba muy nervioso. Hemos hecho un gran partido como equipo. Y ver el pabellón así es algo digno de recordar", dijo el internacional español en declaraciones a 'DAZN'.

articles.summary: The Indiana Fever had their three-game win streak snapped on Sunday with a 93-77 loss to the Washington Mystics.
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever had their three-game win streak snapped on Sunday with a 93-77 loss to the Washington Mystics.

Fever star guard Catilin Clark had a game-high 25 points, but it wasn't enough to overcome Mystics star Kiki Iriafen's 21-point, 14-rebound double-double. Indiana guard Sophie Cunningham was held scoreless in seven minutes off the bench.

The game quickly got out of hand for the Fever, as they never held a lead and fell behind 34-19 by the end of the first quarter. The Mystics led by as many as 26 points as they embarrassed their opponents in front of their home fans at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis.

Still, there were some highlights for Indiana, as star guard Kelsey Mitchell became just the sixth player in WNBA history to reach 800 career three-pointers made.

Clark and the Fever (27-15) will try to get back on track when they face the league-leading Minnesota Lynx (32-10) on Tuesday.

articles.title: New NBA Trade Rumors Reveal Potential Buddy Hield Landing Spot After Midseason Hawks-Warriors Deal
articles.summary: After joining the Atlanta Hawks halfway through the 2025-26 campaign, Buddy Hield could be on the move again.
articles.body:
After joining the Atlanta Hawks halfway through the 2025-26 campaign, Buddy Hield could be on the move again.

Per NBA insider Jake Fischer , the Hawks "have engaged in on-and-off trade discussions" with the Charlotte Hornets regarding the veteran sharpshooter. Fischer noted that such discussions have also included Dorian Finney-Smith, who was traded to Charlotte earlier this offseason.

Fischer noted that earlier this offseason, the Hawks proposed a trade that included Devin Carter, but Atlanta ended up waiving the former lottery pick earlier this month. Carter has since signed with the Boston Celtics.

Hield is coming off a season in which he put up just 7.6 points per game on 43.7 percent from the field and 34.9 percent from deep. It marked the worst statistical season of his career.

While Hield's production has steadily declined over the past few years, he's still a relatively reliable three-point shooter off the bench. The Hornets could use him for a quick spark when its starting rotation comes out.

Trading Hield would help the Hawks shed his $9.65 million salary for the upcoming season, as well as his $10.09 million player option for the 2027-28 campaign. Atlanta perhaps isn't desperate to do so, as it is still $11.5 million under the first apron, per Spotrac .

Finney-Smith is coming off an injury-riddled season that saw him play just 37 games, putting up 3.3 points per game for the Houston Rockets. The Rockets dealt Finney-Smith and three future second-round picks to the Hornets in July in return for cash considerations.

While Finney-Smith was far from his best last season, he'd give the Hawks another defensive option on the wing as they look to compete in the playoffs again.

articles.title: New Knicks Rumors Reveal Mike Brown's Stance on James Wiseman After Center's Recent Contract
articles.summary: The New York Knicks signed five veteran players to Exhibit 9 training camp contracts this past week, opening up a battle for the final roster spot (or two) between wings John Konchar, Bruce Brown and Ochai Agbaji and big men Drew Eubanks and James Wiseman.
articles.body:
The New York Knicks signed five veteran players to Exhibit 9 training camp contracts this past week, opening up a battle for the final roster spot (or two) between wings John Konchar, Bruce Brown and Ochai Agbaji and big men Drew Eubanks and James Wiseman.

According to NBA insider Marc Stein , "It's believed that the Knicks will only fill one of the two current vacancies in terms of the maximum 15 standard contracts they can carry starting Opening Night (Oct. 21) unless they make another roster move first that sheds salary."

Wiseman is a name to watch. Knicks' head coach Mike Brown was an assistant with the Golden State Warriors during Wiseman's first two NBA seasons and "word is that Brown, furthermore, is indeed a Wiseman fan. The newly crowned champs likewise do appear to have a clear need for a third big man behind Karl-Anthony Towns and Andre Drummond."

Wiseman, 25, appeared in just five games over the past two seasons for the Indiana Pacers after suffering a torn left Achilles in the 2024-25 season opener. In total, he's averaged just nine points and 5.5 rebounds in 152 career games since being the No. 2 overall pick in the 2020 NBA draft.

His history with Brown and the team's need for a third center gives him a chance to earn a roster berth, though he's going to have plenty of competition come training camp.

articles.title: NBA injury update: $40 million Golden State Warriors star gets positive news after devastating first season with the franchise
articles.summary: NBA News: Kristaps Porzingis joined the Warriors at the trade deadline as a key piece, and his first stretch in Golden State never got going. Illness and injuri.
articles.body: Kristaps Porzingis joined the Warriors at the trade deadline as a key piece, and his first stretch in Golden State never got going. Illness and injuries kept taking games away, and the year closed with more questions than answers.The $40 million star has spent the summer insisting the mystery illness is in the past. Now a new assistant coach and the general manager are backing that optimism with their own words, and one of them has a very specific plan for the big man. Media Day arrives on Sept. 28, so the first live answers are close.Warriors' Kristaps Porzingis gets positive health updateKristaps Porzingis has sent the same message all summer. The 2024 NBA champion has said more than once that the "mystery illness" is behind the Latvian, and that a full season feels realistic.The staff now sounds like it agrees. Frank Vogel, the new assistant on Steve Kerr's bench, made it plain. "I'm really excited about putting him in my defensive system," Vogel told Luca Evans of the San Francisco Chronicle. Vogel said the scheme is packed with details he believes in, and that shot-blocking bigs get a lot out of it. He looks forward to putting Porzingis in those spots.On paper, the pairing with Draymond Green stands out. A front line of Porzingis and Green could cause opponents real trouble, particularly if Gui Santos, De'Anthony Melton and rookie Yaxel Lendeborg deliver on the perimeter. Golden State finished 11th in the league on defense last year, and this group projects to be better than average.General manager Mike Dunleavy sees it the same way. The team studied the problem at length, Dunleavy told the Chronicle, looking at how to help and how to do better. The things the staff discussed and worked through, he said, "lean in the direction of him having a healthier year."Camp will offer the first real evidence. Media Day is set for Sept. 28, and the Warriors train at BYU-Hawaii from Sept. 29 through Oct. 3. The team has already signed Nick Boyd, Elias Ralph and Obi Agbim to training camp deals, and the 15-man roster is expected to be final in the first week of October.Kristaps Porzingis' first season with Warriors was devastatingIt is easy to see why the Warriors are welcoming good news. Golden State thought the trade deadline had delivered a key piece, and the closing stretch of the regular season said otherwise.Porzingis missed 16 games over that stretch and played in only 15, thanks to a mix of injuries and illnesses. The Latvian big man was more often out than in, which is a tough way to start life with a new team.The play-in tournament brought a bit of hope and then a setback. Porzingis looked good in the win over the Clippers, a sign of what the Warriors had been hoping to get. Against the Suns, right ankle soreness held Porzingis to 15 minutes in the final play-in loss. Fifteen games to close the regular season, then fifteen minutes in the final play-in game.Golden State opens the preseason against the Clippers in Honolulu on Oct. 4, then starts the regular season against the Lakers on Oct. 21 at Crypto.com Arena.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Luka Doncic gets emotional with heartfelt message to his daughters ahead of Lakers return as NBA star shares a personal family moment with fans
articles.summary: NBA News: Luka Doncic left basketball out of his newest Instagram post and wrote to his two daughters instead. He shared it on Sunday, after spending a big part.
articles.body: Luka Doncic left basketball out of his newest Instagram post and wrote to his two daughters instead. He shared it on Sunday, after spending a big part of the offseason in Slovenia and getting back to Los Angeles.The note was short and carried no news about the team. Even so, the calendar gives it weight. Lakers media day is Sept. 28, and training camps around the league open the next day. The Slovenian picked his family as the audience before any of that began, and he kept the words plain.Luka Doncic shares heartfelt message to his daughters ahead of Lakers returnThe Sept. 20 post was written in Slovenian. Translated into English, its main line reads: “Wherever I go, you are always with me. I love you!”G+O, the daughters' initials, sits at the top of the caption. Doncic also told them that being apart will not change where they stand in his life. Two heart emojis wrap it up. Nothing in it points to the season or his workouts. It reads like a dad checking in, and little else.His daughters were already part of his summer plans. As Reuters reported in May, he chose to skip Slovenia's national-team duty to have more time with them. The 2025-26 season had ended without him on the floor for the playoffs, since a left hamstring injury sidelined him.The Lakers star also used Ljubljana as a small training base. In August, he brought teammates together there for bonding and a pair of casual practices. September brought his own conditioning and court work in the same city. The August meetups gave the group a head start on familiarity before the official preseason.Coach JJ Redick will soon start testing how the roster works around Doncic, and the rotation will take shape from there.Luka Doncic shares honest take on his growth on and off the courtDoncic enters this season as the lone headliner in Los Angeles, with LeBron James gone. In an interview with SLAM, he talked about how he has changed. His answer was modest, “probably a better basketball player, more mature.” The way he plays, smile included, is much the same, he added.Madrid is where his pro career started. From there he moved to the NBA and was ranked among its best in short order. Going pro early was not easy, yet he credits it with pushing him to mature faster than most players.Dallas is part of the growth story as well. Boston beat the Mavericks in the 2024 NBA Finals, and Doncic was the one leading Dallas there. Doubts about his leadership, and about whether he could win a title, followed.Los Angeles has already seen the fun side. In one full season with the Lakers, fans and teammates noticed his lively personality, the way he needles opponents and hunts for any competitive edge.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body:
The Las Vegas Aces remained in the running for the No. 2 seed in the WNBA playoffs following Sunday's 98-77 in over the Seattle Storm, though it remains a long shot.

Because the Aces hold the tiebreaker over the Golden State Valkyries, they would earn the No. 2 seed if both teams finish tied in the standings. That would require two more Las Vegas wins and two more Valkyries losses, however.

Given that Golden State is still in the running for the top seed—and has very winnable games against Portland and Los Angeles remaining—the Aces are more likely playing to maintain the No. 3 seed ahead of the Atlanta Dream.

Here's a full look at the updated standings following Sunday's scores :

All playoff berths have been clinched. Only postseason seeding is yet to be determined.

The playoff seeding remains very much in flux. Indiana, for instance, could finish anywhere between No. 3 and No. 8 depending on how the regular season concludes. Sunday's loss against the Washington Mystics was particularly brutal given that the Fever finish their season with two matchups against the Minnesota Lynx.

"Every one of these games that we're playing right now are like playoff games," Fever head coach Stephanie White told reporters following Sunday's loss. "We've got to understand collectively that everything has to take it up a notch. Intensity level. Preparation. Knowing personnel on our scouting report. At this time of the year, it's not meant to be pretty basketball. It's meant to be gritty basketball, and I think we have to be open to understanding that that's the case. We got knocked in the mouth [against the Mystics]."

So much is left to be decided in the final week of the WNBA regular season. Buckle up.

articles.title: WNBA Legend Lisa Leslie's Statue Unveiled Outside of Sparks' Arena in New Videos, Photos
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Sparks officially unveiled a statue honoring WNBA legend Lisa Leslie outside of the Crypto.com Arena on Sunday.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Sparks officially unveiled a statue honoring WNBA legend Lisa Leslie outside of the Crypto.com Arena on Sunday.

"First of all, she's cute," Leslie said after seeing her statue for the first time. "I was so worried. I did not want to look like a linebacker up here. But she's cute. I wanted to make sure that this statue was a perfect blend of fearlessness and the competitor that I was and I am and I'll always be. But also... I wore my ribbons, I had my nails polished, which y'all can't see, but the girl got her polish on because I never wanted the boys or the men to think that I was a boy. I wanted to play hard like them, but I wanted them to know that I respected myself and that I was a lady. And I wanted for little girls to see my ribbons when I played because I wanted them to be able to see themselves in me."

Leslie, 54, was a three-time WNBA MVP during her 12-year career, winning a pair of championships with the Sparks. She was elected to the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame in 2015.

articles.body: Luka Doncic regresa a Estados Unidos tras haber pasado gran parte de postemporada en Eslovenia. articles.title: Lisa Leslie, la 'Primera Dama' del baloncesto: la pionera en machacar ya se codea con Kobe, Magic, Shaq...
articles.standfirst: Primera jugadora de las Sparks en tener una estatua en el Star Plaza del Crypto.com Arena
articles.summary: Primera jugadora de las Sparks en tener una estatua en el Star Plaza del Crypto.com Arena
articles.body: La pionera Lisa Leslie, la primera mujer en realizar un mate en un partido de la WNBA, la primera jugadora de la liga en firmar con una agencia de modelos y, ahora es la primera jugadora de Los Angeles Sparks en ser inmortalizada con una estatua de bronce frente al Crypto.com Arena. Leslie (54 años y 1,96 m.) se convirtió en la decimosexta persona homenajeada con una estatua en lo que se conoce como Star Plaza, durante una ceremonia que contó con la presencia leyendas de Los Angeles Lakers como Magic Johnson, Byron Scott, James Worthy o Michael Cooper; y su excompañera de equipo en las Sparks y también miembro del Salón de la Fama, Candace Parker. "Estaba preocupada, pero se ve bien", comentó Leslie al ver por primera vez la estatua de bronce de 3,3 metros) que recrea su icónico mate. La estatua de Leslie se alza sobre un pedestal y lleva por nombre 'The First Lady' (La Primera Dama). La estatua de Leslie fue creada por el escultor Omri Amrany y la artista Julie Rotblatt Amrany. Lisa Leslie comentó que "quería asegurarme de que esta estatua fuera una mezcla perfecta de valentía y del espíritu competitivo que tenía, que tengo y que siempre tendré. Pero también... llevaba mis lazos y las uñas pintadas —algo que ustedes no pueden ver, pero que me hice—, porque nunca quise que los chicos o los hombres pensaran que yo era un chico. Quería jugar con intensidad, como ellos, pero también quería que supieran que me respetaba a mí misma y que era una dama". La primera mujer homenajeada en el Star Plaza fue Gigi Bryant, quien falleció junto a su padre, Kobe Bryant, en un accidente de helicóptero en 2020. "Estoy justo enfrente de mi hermanito, Kobe. Estoy justo enfrente de Kobe. Estoy justo al lado de Magic. Personas que han aportado tanto a mi vida. No me canso de decirlo. Quedar inmortalizada aquí en Hollywood... es también un legado duradero del que mis antepasados se sentirían orgullosos", dijo Leslie, señalando la estatua de Bryant al otro lado de la plaza. A lo largo de sus 12 años de carrera en la WNBA, Leslie fue nombrada MVP de la liga en tres ocasiones y llevó a las Sparks a ganar los campeonatos de 2001 y 2002. En 2015, fue incluida en el Salón de la Fama del Baloncesto Naismith.

articles.title: La sequía del Barça no cesa: 0/13 en títulos
articles.standfirst: Los azulgranas suman tres temporadas en blanco y han comenzado la presente perdiendo la final de la Supercopa Endesa, aunque en la revolución del verano hay mimbres para construir
articles.summary: Los azulgranas suman tres temporadas en blanco y han comenzado la presente perdiendo la final de la Supercopa Endesa, aunque en la revolución del verano hay mimbres para construir
articles.body: La Supercopa Endesa prolongó la larga sequía de títulos del Barcelona. Los azulgranas alcanzaron la final, pero con una plantilla llena de caras nuevas, no les dio para derrotar al Asisa Joventut y a Nico Laprovittola, al que dejaron ir en verano. "Sin duda que estaba más motivado por ser contra el Barça. Me costó muchísimo asimilarlo este verano", dijo el base. Sal en la herida. Así que el terrible balance del Barcelona llega a 0/13 en títulos durante las últimas tres campañas y en el inicio de la presente. Hay que remontarse a la Liga Endesa de 2023 para encontrar el último éxito de los culés. Parece la Prehistoria: el entrenador era Sarunas Jasikevicius y la estrella, Nikola Mirotic, recién fichado por el Valencia Basket. El Barça tiene el atenuante de las 11 caras nuevas que han llegado a la plantilla además de Aleksander Sekulic, nuevo inquilino en el banquillo. Se trata de la mayor revolución que haya acometido la sección de baloncesto. Imposible que todas las piezas encajen con solo una pretemporada y unos cuantos amistosos. El equipo, sin duda, será mejor e irá a más con el paso de las semanas. Hay algunos mimbres para ello, como ya se vio en los dos encuentros de la Supercopa. Tyrese Martin apunta a diferencial. Destila calidad, desborda en el uno contra uno y tiene buen físico. Es carne de NBA. De esos jugadores que, a poco que haga -y apunta a hacer mucho-, se sabe que cruzarán el Atlántico de vuelta. Un caso como el del exmadridista Trey Lyles. Justin Robinson tuvo buenos minutos, aunque demostró ser un base con mucha más capacidad ofensiva que de dirección. Olivier Nkamhoua tiene un físico tremendo, puede jugar por encima del aro, carga el rebote con fiereza, entiende el juego y puede ponerse al '5'. Y Josh Nebo será la referencia interior. De sus seis canastas en la Supercopa, cuatro fueron mates. Una mole de 2,06 y casi lo mismo de ancho, aunque puede sufrir con rivales que le aventajen en muchos centímetros. Imposible que no venga a la cabeza Edy Tavares. De los cuatro jugadores que continúan de la temporada pasada, galones para Joel Parra. Ya se le vio ponerse en primera fila en la pretemporada y ha confirmado ese protagonismo en la Supercopa. Kevin Punter seguirá ejerciendo de 'killer', una opción para darle los balones más calientes. Darío Brizuela, que se lastimó en un amistoso, ha dejado destellos y volverá a ser un microondas. Juan Núñez apenas ha tenido siete minutos en el torneo. Lo que haga el Barça para intentar por fin abrir las vitrinas de la sección dependerá de su músculo. La mutación se ha notado sobre todo en la llegada de jugadores mucho más físicos y más jóvenes que los que había. Una dura defensa y dominio del rebote para marcar un ritmo alto son las principales consignas de un Sekulic que tratará de hacer lo que no pudieron Roger Grimau, Joan Peñarroya y Xavi Pascual en su regreso al Palau: ganar un título. Próximo objetivo, la Copa.

articles.title: Ranking 5 NBA Teams With the Worst Salary-Cap Situations
articles.summary: NBA general managers often use the buzzword "optionality" to describe moves that preserve cap flexibility. Some teams, like the Brooklyn Nets, keep it for years as they navigate a difficult rebuild.
articles.body:
NBA general managers often use the buzzword "optionality" to describe moves that preserve cap flexibility. Some teams, like the Brooklyn Nets, keep it for years as they navigate a difficult rebuild.

Others, like the New York Knicks and Oklahoma City Thunder, build championship squads that get increasingly hard to keep together. Their current elite status gives them a pass, since flexibility matters less than going for it—not to mention the Thunder still have plenty of draft compensation to replenish their expensive roster with younger, cheaper players.

The teams that lock themselves in as second-tier contenders are more problematic. The obvious answer to their placement on this list is to win it all, but can the following four semi-contenders—plus the LA Clippers, who have their own issues—prove their difficult cap positions are justified?

The Cleveland Cavaliers will pay Donovan Mitchell and Evan Mobley a combined $133 million in 2029-30. The franchise is committed to its roster, with James Harden, Jarrett Allen, and Peyton Watson. Depth is marginal; Cleveland is just under its first apron hard cap, and flexibility won't open for several years.

Still, the Cavaliers were the second-best team in the East last year, falling to the Knicks in the Conference Finals. They're good enough to boast fifth on the list, but don't get it twisted; the margins are razor-thin.

Cleveland sent out most of its draft capital to build this roster. With its 2033 first-round pick frozen for climbing over last year's second apron, the Cavaliers can offer swaps in 2028 (the lower of an already swapped pick), 2030, and 2032. The only second-rounder available is in 2033.

If the team falls short, its path to improvement may come only through trading away its top-five players.

The Los Angeles Lakers need the trio of Luka Dončić, Austin Reaves, and Walker Kessler to work, after going all-in this summer by paying Reaves a near-max four-year deal and sending their remaining draft capital to acquire Walker Kessler in a trade with the Utah Jazz.

The clock is running on Dončić, who is locked in for only two more seasons, with a player option before the 2028-29 campaign. As long as he's bought in, the Lakers have one of the league's top offensive creators. But if the team struggles, will Dončić start thinking about a new home?

On paper, the Lakers' current ceiling is third in the Western Conference behind the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder. That's best-case, given the gauntlet of talent L.A. will need to fight through to win at the highest level. For the foreseeable future, the Lakers are spent.

The team has just one first-round swap available to offer—outside of trading low-value additional swaps on previously swapped picks. The team has only three second-round selections available—two from the Washington Wizards, both starting in 2031—which may help smaller deals get done, but may not help land a needle-mover.

Improvements will need to come via small free-agent signings or trades where the Lakers' outgoing talent or willingness to take on other unwanted salaries will drive deals more than the squad's meager draft capital.

If the LA Clippers have greater flexibility than the Lakers, they don't have a talent like Dončić to build around.

Overall, the Clippers are in a tough spot, self-imposed after the NBA's investigation into improper sponsorship agreements involving Kawhi Leonard cost them five first-round picks. The team needs a franchise player to build around; acquiring that piece will be the real challenge.

The Clippers recouped a pair of firsts and seconds (plus a first-round swap) by trading Leonard to the Toronto Raptors. But LA is bound by the Stepien rule, making Toronto's 2031 and 2033 firsts untradeable—though they can offer them as swaps. Still, the team has five first-round picks over the next seven years, though none can be dealt outright and the next three are subject to swaps from prior deals. LA also has 4-5 second-rounders available.

Conversely, the Clippers have a relatively clean set of salaries on the books. Darius Garland and Brandon Ingram will earn $86.8 million combined for 2027-28 on expiring contracts, though Ingram can opt out in June. With Rui Hachimura's $14 million team option, Keaton Wagler is the next highest-paid player locked in at $10.2 million for 2027-28.

The team can try to cash out veterans in trades before the February deadline to add more draft compensation, while increasing flexibility to chase top free agents in 2027 and/or 2028. That said, will the recent punishment deter stars from joining the Clippers?

Compared to others on the list, the Orlando Magic are in a better spot. Still, their heavy commitment to a good but not great roster puts them at No. 2. The Magic are in a similar position to the Cavaliers, invested in their core, except the Magic haven't gotten out of the first round since 2010.

The team spent heavily on Paolo Banchero, Franz Wagner, Desmond Bane (via trade), Jalen Suggs, and Wendell Carter Jr. Next, Anthony Black is eligible for an extension; otherwise, he'll hit restricted free agency in July 2027. For a franchise that doesn't pay luxury taxes, the team is looking at a $33 million bill for 2026-27. Keeping Black past this year, barring cost-cutting trades, will lock the Magic into apron territory.

A healthy roster would go a long way, the team's greatest obstacle in recent seasons. Perhaps new head coach Sean Sweeney can get more out of the group than Jamahl Mosley, who was let go in May. The New Orleans Pelicans quickly hired Mosley, but Sweeney will face the same obstacles with a pair of talented forwards who occupy similar space on the court. Still, neither is a reliable floor-spacing shooter from three-point range.

While salaries are high, the Magic have some available draft capital to trade for either their 2032 or 2033 first-round pick; otherwise, the team is limited to swaps in 2027, 2031, and one of 2032/33. Orlando also has 6-7 second-rounders.

The Denver Nuggets, with Nikola Jokić, feel like the Milwaukee Bucks before trading Giannis Antetokounmpo. After winning a title, both franchises have failed to stay on top with their elite star, seemingly getting worse each season.

Will Jokić follow the same path, pushing the Nuggets to trade him or walk as a free agent next July, when he can opt out of his final year at $62.8 million? Or if he re-signs with Denver on a long-term contract, can the franchise rejuvenate around him?

Letting Peyton Watson go to the Cavaliers may have made financial sense, but the Nuggets didn't have to sign and trade him to Cleveland. Denver couldn't justify paying out an additional $200 million in salary and repeater taxes for the young forward. That may make sense, but the future first-round pick from the Cavs won't help Jamal Murray, Jokić, and the rest of the roster anytime soon.

Denver may find a trade with that selection, but the franchise still owes three firsts to the Oklahoma City Thunder (two) and the Brooklyn Nets. Outside of swaps and the Cavaliers' selection in 2031, the Nuggets have 4-5 seconds to offer.

Meanwhile, Denver has hefty obligations to Aaron Gordon, Christian Braun, Murray, and, if Jokić re-signs, that flexibility won't improve anytime soon.

articles.title: Ex-LSU star Flau'Jae Johnson sets Seattle Storm franchise records
articles.summary: Former LSU women's basketball forward Flau'Jae Johnson etched her name in the Seattle Storm record books.
articles.body:
Flau'Jae Johnson continues to shine in her first WNBA season. The former LSU women's basketball star made history for the Seattle Storm , becoming the first rookie in franchise history to score 500 points and make 50 three-pointers in a single season.

Johnson surpassed the mark by scoring 20 points against the Toronto Tempo . She shot 60% from the field while adding three rebounds and two assists. She has started all 39 games she appeared in for the Storm, averaging 14.3 points per game on 40% shooting.

Johnson's All-Rookie campaign looks bright. Her points per game, 559 total points, 51 total steals, and 28 total blocks all rank second among 2026 rookies. Former Notre Dame guard and current Minnesota Lynx guard Olivia Miles is the frontrunner for that award.

The Golden State Valkyries selected Johnson with the No. 8 overall pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft, but they traded her to the Storm later in the draft. She played four seasons at LSU under head coach Kim Mulkey.

articles.title: Tavares: un MVP para disipar cualquier duda
articles.standfirst: El pívot demostró en la SuperCup de la Euroliga que también encaja en el baloncesto de Pedro Martínez, el entrenador que le hizo debutar en la élite hace 13 años
articles.summary: El pívot demostró en la SuperCup de la Euroliga que también encaja en el baloncesto de Pedro Martínez, el entrenador que le hizo debutar en la élite hace 13 años
articles.body: Las dudas que pudiera haber en cuanto a cómo encajaría Edy Tavares en el baloncesto de Pedro Martínez se han disipado con los primeros dos partidos oficiales del Real Madrid. El galardón de MVP conseguido por el pívot en la SuperCup de la Euroliga responde a todas las preguntas: seguirá siendo determinante. Habrá que repartir méritos en esta cuestión. Tavares se lesionó a finales de abril. Sufrió una lesión en el ligamento lateral interno de la rodilla izquierda en el primer partido de la serie de playoffs de la Euroliga ante el Hapoel Tel Aviv y se perdió lo que restaba de temporada. Desde el primer día comenzó a trabajar pensando en la recuperación y, tras conocerse la llegada de Pedro Martínez, también en mejorar su físico para poder adaptarse al ritmo que exige el técnico. El pívot, muy comprometido con la selección de Cabo Verde, llegó a renunciar a disputar unas Ventanas FIBA para seguir mejorando en su preparación. A la pretemporada llegó en perfecto estado de revista. Por números, ya fue el mejor en el primer amistoso ante el Río Breogán. En los primeros partidos oficiales, en la Supercup de Abu Dabi, se le ha visto tan fuerte como siempre, pero más rápido. Nada de quedarse atrás. En alguna jugada fue el primero en llegar al contraataque. Ante el Dubai Basketball se fue por encima de los 31 minutos para hacer 20 puntos, siete rebotes y 22 de valoración. En la final contra el Olympiacos, lastrado por las faltas, jugó casi 20 minutos y acabó con seis puntos, siete capturas y siete créditos de valoración. Entre los dos partidos, +22 con él en pista. Un MVP tan justo como apretado, por el juego coral del Madrid. Y el mérito también es de Pedro Martínez, que ha demostrado saber aprovechar a Tavares no sólo por su altura. Es más sencillo cuando se conoce a la otra parte a la perfección. Fue el técnico catalán quien hizo debutar a Tavares en la ACB un 6 de enero de 2013, cuando dirigía al Gran Canaria. Llevaba poco tiempo jugando al baloncesto, pero apuntaba alto. "Soy un tronco si no acabo sacando algo bueno de este chico", llegó a decir Martínez entonces. Años después, Tavares se iría a la NBA y, tras no tener apenas oportunidades, regresaría en 2017 para enrolarse en el Madrid. Aquella operación cambiaría el destino del baloncesto europeo porque desde entonces el pívot el jugador más determinante del continente. Lo fue con Pablo Laso, con Chus Mateo, con Sergio Scariolo y, como demuestra el MVP, todo apunta a que lo será también con Pedro Martínez, con el que coincide 13 años después. "Él confió en mí cuando nadie lo hacía", dijo Edy tras recibir el galardón este domingo. En un baloncesto que ha cambiado tanto desde entonces, en el que se juega a toda velocidad y en el que se ha multiplicado el uso del triple, Tavares sigue siendo una pieza capital. Es el mismo jugador diferencial que intimida a los rivales, pero con el tiempo ha ganado importancia en ataque y, gracias a su mejora en el pase, se ha convertido en un gran distribuidor: balón dentro y pase fuera hacia uno de sus compañeros, casi siempre colocado en el triple. Puede hincharse a dar asistencias. A sus 34 años y con tres temporadas aún de contrato, podrán llegar fichajes estelares cada verano, pero la era de Tavares en el Real Madrid seguirá vigente.
